arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Blatt argued common law allows late sworn statements to fix complaints.
She claimed the agency adopted this rule in 1966.
Mr. Bell argued the agency cannot override clear statutory language.
He stated the law requires charges to be under oath immediately.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether a job bias complaint survives if it lacks a sworn statement at first. A later sworn statement may fix the error under agency rules. The college claims the law requires the oath from the start.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines how strictly courts enforce sworn statement rules in job bias cases. It affects whether complainants can fix minor filing errors later. It shapes the power of agencies to set procedural rules.
